output.summary: Turnover rose far more than in-state peers (28% to 47% vs 33% to 38%), and the rise is not a migration artifact, since both years reconcile to payroll. Monthly separations stepped up in March 2026, when the two-Saturday policy took effect at all branches. They stepped up again slightly after the April ShiftWise go-live. Pay was cited at a similar share in both years' exit surveys, and no current market data exists. Manager-of-record data is corrupted, so manager blame is untestable. A 15% raise is irreversible and unjustified now. Performance plans based on bad data would punish the wrong people. Pull the branch-level separations and the pay benchmark before December 10.
